about: StepAmounts (#101): the words that decide whether a step's mention of an ingredient gets the line's amount ('Add the carrots' reads 'Add 2 carrots'). All lowercase; an entry ending in an apostrophe ('l'') is elided onto the next word. articles: replaced by the amount. partWords: a step that already says how much, right before the mention or before its article ('half the butter', 'the remaining sugar', '1 cup of the flour', 'a carrot'); the mention stays as written. before: words that may come right before a mention with no article ('Stir in flour', 'with salt', 'and sugar', 'Add flour'); a mention after any other word ('rice flour' when the recipe lists only flour) stays as written, unless that word starts the sentence (an imperative verb). after: words that may follow a mention ('the carrots and celery'); any other word ('the flour mixture', 'the lemon juice') means a longer, different name, so it stays as written. anyWordAfter: true where compounds are written as one word (German), so a following word never extends the name. splitWords: words after the name in a line that mean its amount is used in parts ('2 cups flour, divided', 'plus more for dusting'), so it is never inserted. plurals: [singular ending, plural ending] pairs, so 'the carrot' is '2 carrots'. lineDescriptors (#254): words a line's name may carry before the name a step uses and still be that ingredient ('the butter' for '6 tbsp very cold unsalted butter', 'the oil' for 'olive oil', 'the stock' for 'beef stock'); any other word ('soy sauce', 'bay leaves', 'lemon juice') makes it a different thing, so 'the sauce' stays as written. Such a mention names every line ending in the step's words, so 'the oil' with olive oil and sesame oil listed names both. Empty in a language that puts modifiers after the noun.
